BACKGROUND INFORMATION The South Bronx Open Space Task Force has an active staff composed of community organizers, architects, landscape architects, and horticulturalists. Nine sites are curruntly being reviewed in accordance with the Uniform Land Use Review procedure. One of the nine sites and parts of two sites will become neighbor- hood land trusts, that is, will be owned by non-profit corporations, in the interests of all neighborhood residents. All designs are the result of parti- cipatory planning, based on prioritized community needs; all construction will be carried out by the community residents; and all future maintenance will be assumed by the responsible community. All other sites are City-owned and will be leased to the community group by the City. For a more detailed description of the proposal, including a list of community groups involved and summaries of the proposed leases, see CPC report C790495PLX, dated March 12, 1980. This application, C790502PLX, requests the lease of City-owned property, Block 2608, Lots 58 & 60, located at Fulton Avenue and East 166th Street in the Bronx, to the South Bronx Roots Community Association, for the development of community open space. The proposed site has already been cultivated as a gardening demonstration area. Some residents of the surrounding tenant-managed properties have planted individual plots as well as contributed to cultivation of a com- munal garden, all with considerable effort and minimal resources. The plans for this site include the continued introduction of new gardening techniques, with the aid of such technical assistance groups as the Cornell Extension Service and the Council on the Environment.
